text:
Alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC — tradeoffs between the view-compiler and the query-fabric for dashboard panels. Need a concise rollout that preserves permission correctness and panel SLOs.

Priya: Recap: view-compiler compiles a tenant-specific plan with permission pushdown (single plan, fewer RPCs). Query-fabric routes to per-service endpoints and applies permissions at the leaf (simpler ownership, more hops).

Mateo: Perf tradeoffs: view-compiler has better p95 under steady-state because it avoids extra network hops and enables aggressive local caching. Query-fabric is safer for rapid schema/UX changes and smaller mental model for teams.

Jen: Observed numbers on staging with the new panel shape:
```
panels: 120
- view-compiler p95: 110ms
- query-fabric p95: 420ms (warmup) / 160ms (steady)
errors: permission-mismatch: 12 (query-fabric path)
```

Alex: Proposal: (1) Keep view-compiler for read-heavy dashboard panels where we can compile stable plans. (2) Implement a permission-vector cache with short TTL (60s) to reduce permission check latency. (3) Fall back to query-fabric when compiler can't produce a plan or on cache miss.

Priya: :thumbsup: Agree with hybrid. We must also preserve auditability — every permission decision needs to be logged (tenant, panel, rule-id).

Mateo: Draft rollout config (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%):
```yaml
rollout:
  strategy: canary
  canary_percentage: 10
  metrics: [panel_p95, permission_error_rate]
  fallback_on_error: true
```

Jen: Operational notes: invalidation semantics are the tricky bit. If an admin changes role bindings we need near-real-time invalidation. Suggest hooking the permission service event stream to push invalidation events for affected permission-vector keys. Also tag panels with SLO class (interactive/async) so the routing policy picks the right path.

deploy-bot: deploy-canary/view-compiler -> success (hash: a1b2c3) :white_check_mark:

Alex: Action items: Priya to prototype permission-vector cache MVP + logging, Mateo to add invalidation hook to event-stream, Jen to label panels with SLO classes and run perf sweep. I'll own the RFC follow-up doc and cut the rollout PR.

Priya: I'll pair with Mateo tomorrow 10am to wire the stream invalidation. Adding to calendar.

Jen: I'll run a 10k synthetic user test on staging and post the dashboard perf results back here.

Alex: Thanks everyone. If anything surprising pops in the perf runs, we revert to query-fabric for the canary and iterate.
